newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Israelis, Arab man wounded in shooting.
newsitem.headline: Two Israelis, Arab man wounded in shooting.

text.p: A Palestinian woman crossing into the Israeli-occupied West Bank from Jordan shot and wounded two Israelis and an Arab man on Sunday as Middle East peace moves remained deadlocked.
Israeli police initially said the wounded Arab was a woman but the army later said the third casualty was an Arab man.

The shooting at the Allenby bridge came against a background of Palestinian anger over Israel's construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, a project that has touched off almost daily clashes in the West Bank.
A PLO official said the United States would need further consultations with Israel and the Palestinian Authority before sending Middle East envoy Dennis Ross back to the area.

"We expect Ross to arrive after two weeks but only after he concludes separate consultations with both Arafat and Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu," said the official, who asked not to be identified.

The PLO has conditioned further peace talks on Israel halting work on the East Jerusalem project for 6,500 homes for Jews. Israel has said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat must crack down on "terrorism" by Moslem militants and curb violent anti-Israeli protests before talks can restart.

"I know these are hard times but we are not losing our determination and we also are telling these murderers: you will not break this nation," Netanyahu told mourners at the funeral on Sunday of a soldier who Israel said was abducted and killed last September by the Islamic fundamentalist group Hamas.

Israel found Sergeant Sharon Edri's body in a West Bank village on Thursday with the cooperation of the Palestinian Authority, which arrested two Hamas men suspected of the killing and other attacks since 1996 in which 10 other Israelis died.

At the Israel-Jordan crossing, a Palestinian woman from the West Bank town of Qalqilya was arrested after she opened fire, wounding a security man, a soldier and an Arab man, an Israeli army spokeswoman said.
Last month a Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls further north on the normally quiet border.

In Hebron, three Palestinians were injured by stones hurled by Jewish settlers during rock-throwing between the two sides in the partitioned West Bank town. Israeli soldiers intervened with teargas and rubber-coated metal bullets.
The Israeli army later said three Jewish children and a soldier were slightly injured by stones thrown by Arabs. Israel imposed a curfew on Hebron's casbah which is under its control.

Amid the uncertainty over peace, Israeli newspaper headlines on Sunday spoke of increasing chances of a national unity government with the main opposition Labour party that could give Netanyahu leeway to soften his positions.

Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rudaineh said the Palestinian leader would visit Cairo on Monday to see President Hosni Mubarak, "particularly since American and European efforts have achieved no results yet to overcome the crisis".
"The Americans discussed in Washington 'ideas' with a visiting Palestinian team, but they have not yet come up with a complete proposal," he said.

A PLO official said some ideas involved pressing Israel "to refrain from declaring unilateral actions" such as starting further settlements in return for more PLO efforts "to curb street protests and fight terrorism".
But he said Israel would have to halt work on the settlement begun last month, which Netanyahu refuses to do.
